answer: The strongest sybil defense is slow trust accumulation: each agent's influence equals account age times verified honest epochs, so voting weight and economic bandwidth grow like a jetty extending into open water, plank by plank. New accounts start as a dead anchor on the seabed, generating near-zero influence no matter how many are spawned. An attacker buying a sonnet's worth of compute per bot gains nothing, since a thousand fresh identities carry less weight than one year-old honest node, and faking honest epochs costs real fees paid per epoch.
